hyps.why: With edge 4 removed, node 1 reaches the output only via edge 2, so a conv on edge 0 contributes less (nothing at all if edge 2 is also none).
If edge 5 is none, node 2 cannot reach the output, so the edit to edge 1 has essentially no effect instead of its usual gain.
Edge 2 feeds node 2, which is cut off from the output when edge 5 is none, so the conv's benefit disappears.
With edge 5 gone, the direct edge carries more of the signal, so adding a conv there gives a larger gain.
Turning a missing direct edge into a residual connection helps, while swapping a conv for skip on that edge removes capacity.
Replacing a 1x1 conv with a 3x3 conv gives a small gain compared with replacing none, skip, or pool.
The edit changes nothing when the edge already holds that op, while on average it improves the other ops.
Removing edge 5 when edge 4 is already none leaves only the direct edge into the output, which badly hurts accuracy.
With edge 5 absent, deleting edge 4 cuts all deep paths, leaving only edge 3 as input to the output node.
If edge 1 is none, removing edge 0 disconnects nodes 1 and 2 from the input and collapses the cell to edge 3 alone.
